method: PRODUCED/CONSUMED parity via rg; seam-catalog lenses (registration parity, call-vs-handler, config-reader, stub sweep); code-smell pass. Read-only — no edits made during review phase.

findings.consumer_location: Zero call sites anywhere in src/, tests/, interfaces/, desktop/. Only the canonical_index field is mutated (register()) and read (the field's other read at the symmetric `canonical_name_of` accessor).
findings.rationale: Pure form-1 dead public API. The accessor was added for log-correlation with a doc comment about it being 'useful for log correlation', but no log emitter, debug tool, or admin RPC actually calls it. The paired `canonical_name_of` (let me verify) is also likely dead. Recommend CUT: if a future caller needs it, the index field is right there. Demoting to pub(crate) is also viable.
findings.residual_risk: Trivial — pure read accessor over an internal index, no live callers.

findings.consumer_location: Zero production call sites. Only used in #[cfg(test)] at src/generation/registry.rs:551, :563. Production callers use `registry.get(name)` and convert to error inline (the error path needs the context-bearing error message that get_or_err does not provide).
findings.rationale: Pure form-1 dead public API. The convenience method is not more convenient: its error is `format!("Provider '{name}' not found in registry")` — which lacks the generation_type context that callers need (e.g. `provider '{name}' for type '{gen_type}' not found`). Demoting to pub(crate) keeps it usable by tests in the same module. Recommend demoting.

findings.produced: parse_generation_requests / has_generation_requests (the only two pub fns in src/generation/response_parser.rs)
findings.consumer_location: Zero production callers. Only used in #[cfg(test)] within the same file (response_parser.rs:120, :133, :143, :152, :161, :165, :172). Re-exported in generation/mod.rs:67 but the re-export points at unused API.
findings.rationale: Pure form-1 dead public API. The `[GENERATE:type:provider:model:prompt]` syntax these functions parse appears nowhere in the production codebase. The factory path is `tool → registry → provider.generate(request)` with `GenerationRequest` constructed by the builtin tools (src/builtin_tools/generation/{image_generate,speech_generate}.rs), not parsed out of model output. Three options: (a) CUT both functions + the test module (which only exercises the parser, not any integration) — purest option; (b) leave the parser in place as 'planned future syntax for inline model-output-embedded generation requests' — this is a spec-time promise with no commit; (c) DECIDE: this was on the roadmap at some point. Recommend DECIDE: if no design doc keeps this contract alive, CUT.
findings.residual_risk: If kept dormant: a future contributor who reads the re-export and assumes model-output parsing is wired will be misled. CUTTING is safe; restoring the module if needed is mechanical.

findings.produced: FalProviderBuilder / MidjourneyProviderBuilder / OpenAiCompatProviderBuilder / ReplicateProviderBuilder (4 pub struct builders + their public methods)
findings.consumer_location: Zero external callers outside src/generation/providers/. Each is only used inside its own provider module (and the factory at factory.rs:158, :252, :243, :217 which calls `.builder()` static methods on the Provider, not the Builder type directly). Re-exported in providers/mod.rs:69, :72, :74, :78.
findings.rationale: All four builders are pub-exported but their only consumers are: (a) the factory.rs create_provider match arm for that provider type, and (b) unit tests in the provider's own module. The factory's pattern is `let mut builder = XProvider::builder(...); ...; builder.build()?` — it never names the Builder type explicitly. Tests do name it. Demoting all four to `pub(crate)` would keep tests compiling (they live in the same crate) and remove the public-API surface that no caller uses. Recommend demoting.
findings.residual_risk: Trivial — provider modules still own their builders; pub(crate) keeps the factory working.

reviewed_no_change.subject: All 20 provider types in src/generation/providers/
reviewed_no_change.evidence: Each provider is constructed by the factory at src/generation/providers/factory.rs:76-291 via a match arm on `provider_type`. The factory is called from src/gateway/handlers/providers/handlers.rs:197, :332 (RPC create_provider_inner) and src/gateway/voice/format.rs:134. Each provider impl registers a `static_voice_list()` method (or equivalent) consumed by `static_voices_for_provider_type` (voice_catalog.rs:42) which is consumed by src/gateway/handlers/generation_providers/voices.rs:199. The 23 #[allow(dead_code)] annotations on fields throughout types.rs files are all `// Deserialized from API response` markers — the fields are populated by serde and surfaced via Debug/log, not by direct Rust access. Valid form-1 exception per the audit playbook.
